newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end higher, profit taking emerges.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end higher, profit taking emerges.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed slightly higher on Monday after a day of volatile trading as profit-taking erased most of the gains that stemmed from hopes of an economic recovery, brokers said.
"Consolidation emerged in the belief that the market was overheated," Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
The composite stock index closed 1.62 points higher at 758.39. It briefly hit a new year high of 770.97.
"Trading volume rose to 84.89 million shares, the highest level this year. That indicates a further consolidation on Tuesday," Na said.
Brokers said the sentencing of 11 people in connection with the Hanbo loan scandal had little impact on the market.
Shares of KEPCO gained 1,000 won to 28,500, thanks largely to foreign buying. Brokers said foreigners bought about 500,000 KEPCO shares.

"The foreign buying seems to be inspired by views that the nation's economy has bottomed," said Kong Hyun-moo, an analyst at ING Baring Securities. About 19 million KEPCO shares are still available for foreign buying. "Foreigners are buying the stock as other blue chips like POSCO and Samsung Electronics (64050.KS sell out," Kong said.
The trade ministry said the nation's customs-cleared trade deficit narrowed sharply to $686 million in May from a $1.44 billion shortfall a year earlier.
But brokers said the shrinking deficit news would have a long-term positive effect.
"We have not seen any rallies in export-related shares. But the news will gradually improve market sentiment," said Lee Young-won, a broker at Daewoo Securities.
Brokers said South Korea's technology shares were hardly affected by the fallout from Intel Corp's drop in the U.S. on Friday.
Intel's surprise announcement that second quarter results would be lower than expected due to weaker demand triggered as massive sell-ofg of Intel and other tech stocks in the U.S.
